steps.prompt:
Use case: compositing / identity-preserve.
Asset type: transparent 4 by 4 sprite-sheet of COMPLETE human HEADS WEARING HELMET 01, game equipment module, NOT empty helmet icons.
Input 1 is the exact helmet equipment design to preserve: olive open three-rib cage, ivory crown straps, dark bands, copper rivets, one ivory side protector on the wearer's LEFT. Input 2 shows the four existing character identities, from left to right: Bastion (brown hair, broad male face), Traqueuse (dark swept hair, narrow female face), Arcaniste (pale white hair, mature male face), Métamorphe (tousled brown hair, face exactly as reference).
Draw a SQUARE image with exactly SIXTEEN isolated neck-up head sprites on genuine transparent alpha in an even 4-column, 4-row grid, generous transparent cell margins, no text, no lines. Rows top to bottom correspond to those four characters in that exact order. Columns left to right: 1 true FRONT facing viewer, 2 true BACK showing the nape with NO FACE, 3 front-three-quarter looking to image LEFT, 4 front-three-quarter looking to image RIGHT. The laterals must BOTH show a little front face, not rear views and not pure side profile. Do not mirror the helmet asymmetry: the ivory protector remains on the same physical left temple in all angles, changing visibility naturally.
Each cell is one finished coherent wearable HEAD module: human head anatomically INSIDE the helmet, matching crown to skull, strap under brow on the forehead, temples enclosed by protectors; preserve the character's face below the brow, with restrained compressed hair inside the cage. Never a separate head offset below or next to an empty helmet. Keep the complete head, chin and a SHORT NARROW NECK ending in a clean horizontal base; no shoulders, clothing, chest, background, pedestal or shadows. Same physical scale and neck baseline across viewpoints of each row, centred by the NECK rather than by the asymmetrical accessory bounding box.
Style: match Project RL reference sprite finish, subdued hand-painted pixel-art RPG texture, crisp small readable forms and clusters, matte worn surfaces, subtle top-left light, dark clean silhouettes. Not vector line art, not smooth 3D, not photorealistic, no large expressive cartoon eyes. This sheet will be conditioned into ~17-pixel-tall head modules in a native64 game. Preserve silhouette readability rather than adding new details. Helmet shape, palette, materials and icon identity invariant across the four character rows. Faces and hair are those of their reference character; do not put Arcaniste's white hair on the other characters.

Use case: compositing / identity-preserve.
Asset type: transparent 4 by 4 sprite-sheet of COMPLETE human HEADS WEARING HELMET 02. Not empty helmets.
Reference image 1 is the blue-grey and ivory helmet with one cyan monocular orbital optic and cyan mast, whose FRONT design must be preserved. Its older lateral views have perspective/side ambiguities; correct those instead of copying errors.
Reference image 2 gives four character identities in order: Bastion broad brown-haired male; Traqueuse narrow dark-haired female; Arcaniste mature white-haired male; Métamorphe tousled brown-haired face. Reference image 3 demonstrates the required exact 4-column 4-row HEAD MODULE sheet layout and appropriate facial rendering ONLY; its olive helmet is a DIFFERENT helmet and must NOT be used here.
Output one SQUARE sheet, exactly 16 isolated complete helmeted heads on genuine transparent alpha. Four equal rows in that identity order. Four columns: FRONT facing viewer; true BACK showing nape without face; moderate front-three-quarter looking image LEFT; moderate front-three-quarter looking image RIGHT. Both lateral views still show much of the front, not profiles or back-three-quarter. Same head size and neck baseline in all four views of each identity. Centre on the narrow NECK, not on helmet accessory bounds. Each head ends in a short dark helmet liner around a narrow anatomical neck, clean horizontal base, no shoulders, torso, clothes, body or background. No labels, lines or shadows.
All helmet pieces belong to ONE object on ONE human head. Fit the helmet skull shell around the skull, the eye opening exactly over the HUMAN EYE line, the nasal bridge on the nose, side guards around cheeks, chin guard around chin. Retain small natural shadowed skin visible only inside the actual openings. No original hair, old cap, second helmet, eye, or face sticking out past the shell. Never put a helmet above, beside, or low across a separate head. Keep crown, nasal bridge, cheek, eye and chin dimensions anatomically coherent across views.
Critical asymmetry: exactly ONE cyan orbital optic and one cyan mast, fixed on the WEARER'S LEFT side. In FRONT both are on IMAGE RIGHT. In BACK the mast is on IMAGE LEFT. In the column looking IMAGE LEFT, that physical left optic is the NEAR-SIDE optic, visibly centred over the left human eye, mast behind it on the image-right side of that head. In the column looking IMAGE RIGHT, the optic is on the FAR eye; show a narrow foreshortened portion just beyond the nasal bridge on the image-left/front side, no duplicate optic on the near temple. Mast stays behind on the far image-left side. Do not mirror the hardware to a different temple. Keep the blue-grey skull panels, angular ivory brow, dark graphite lower mask, copper-free pale materials, cyan glass, and helmet identity.
Style: subdued hand-painted pixel-art tactical RPG sprite, crisp clustered shading, worn matte metal, subtle top-left light, restrained faces matching reference identities, dark readable silhouette. No glossy 3D, anime eyes or vector art. Intended as ~17-pixel tall native64 game head modules. Prioritise coherent wearable shape and clean silhouettes over decorative detail.

Use case: precise-object-edit / identity-preserve.
The blue helmet head sheet (reference 1) mistakenly has both lateral columns looking toward image RIGHT. We need an EIGHT-HEAD corrective sprite sheet with TWO COLUMNS and FOUR ROWS, genuine transparent background, no text or guides. Keep its front/back views in the original file untouched; this output contains ONLY the corrected laterals.
Rows: Bastion brown-haired broad male; Traqueuse dark-haired female; Arcaniste mature white-haired male; Métamorphe tousled brown-haired male, matching the faces in reference 1. Keep the SAME exact blue-grey/ivory helmet 02 and the heads from reference 1. Reference 2 is an ORIENTATION GUIDE ONLY: copy the two opposite face directions seen in its 3rd and 4th columns, but DO NOT copy its olive cage helmet.
LEFT COLUMN: each human NOSE clearly projects toward the LEFT EDGE of the image, their face and gaze look LEFT in a moderate front-three-quarter. We see their physical LEFT cheek and LEFT temple as the near side on IMAGE RIGHT of that head. Its ONE cyan monocular is over that near left eye, prominently visible on the IMAGE RIGHT temple. Its antenna mast sits behind that optic at the near rear right side. The broad visible ear protector is also on this near right side of the head, nose projects left.
RIGHT COLUMN: the SAME head turns the opposite way, NOSE clearly projects toward the RIGHT EDGE of the image, face and gaze look RIGHT in a moderate front-three-quarter. The visible near temple/ear is now the character's RIGHT temple and has NO monocular and NO mast. The single physical LEFT-eye monocular must be partially visible as a NARROW CYAN STRIP BEYOND THE NOSE BRIDGE ON IMAGE LEFT, attached to the far eye, not a duplicated large near-side goggle on the right. The same mast remains behind the skull on its FAR IMAGE LEFT rear side. Do not move this hardware to the near right temple.
Critical: one character must face LEFT in the left column and RIGHT in the right column. Opposite nose silhouettes, no two right-facing heads in one row. Helmet asymmetry remains on the wearer's LEFT anatomical side. Correct the perspective, not by mirroring the entire sprite.
Complete clean skull/helmet/face/short narrow neck as ONE wearable head module. No chest, torso, shoulders or old head underneath. Same neck height and physical size within each row, centred by neck. Fully transparent cell margins. Same readable subdued RPG pixel-art cluster style as reference 1; no vector art, big cartoon eyes, shiny 3D or added accessories. Preserve metal panels, brow, chin guard, palette and all identity details.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target image 1 is a complete 4x4 helmeted-head sprite sheet. Reference image 2 is the exact accepted helmet design. Make ONE TARGETED correction: restore the original helmet's DARK GRAPHITE CENTRAL NASAL / LOWER FACE GUARD to the FRONT and both front-three-quarter heads in each row. The central guard in reference 2 runs from the nasal bridge down over the nose and mouth to the chin, a dark tapered angular panel. The target currently exposes almost the whole face and lost that important original protective part.
Add this coherent central graphite nasal and mouth guard inside the same pale cheek/chin framework, fitted to the human face underneath and matching the projected nose direction in each view. Retain naturally visible small eye and cheek areas at the sides, the single cyan optic over the wearer's left eye, and every existing helmet opening/side guard as close as possible to reference2. Preserve blue-grey crown, ivory angled brow/temple panels, graphite inset, cyan orbital lens and mast. Do not invent a new wide goggle, a second optic, teeth, jaw vents or extra accessories.
Everything else must stay the same: EXACT same sixteen head identities, layout, physical size, short narrow necks, skin/hair, row order, fully transparent background, front/back/left/right column directions. Third column noses point LEFT; fourth column noses point RIGHT. Preserve the small far-side cyan lens and far-side mast positions from target's fourth column. Leave BACK column unchanged. No shoulders or torso. Do not regenerate face poses or add scenery, shadows, labels, glow or text. Maintain the same small readable painted RPG sprite texture. This is a wearable head module, not a floating empty helmet pasted on a second head.

invariants: Existing approved icons unchanged. Closed models03..05 keep their existing authored shells; open models01/02 become complete wearable head modules.
conditioning: prepare_helmet_head_units.py: explicit row segmentation, head-neck alignment, aspect-preserving native scaling, alpha component conditioning, no RGB painting
